title: Change mentions of "member" to "property" where appropriate
body:
See also a [RocketChat discussion](https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/documentation/thread/tPE9nBS6iKFaX2WJm), if it were to embed properly.

Many spots in the class reference say "_member_" when they either _really_ mean to say "_property_" or "_member variable_".
"Member" is almost always incorrect for reasons explained below. But, there's a bunch of annoying nuance between "property" or "member variable".
So I did make up my mind and, **as far as Godot is concerned**, I think that:

- A "_member_" is _anything_ belonging to an object ~~or class~~. Properties, signals, methods, constants, even inner classes, etc. are all members.
	- Local variables and local constants[^1] are **not** members.
	- This is not particularly controversial, but it's worth keeping in mind nonetheless.
- A "_member variable_" is one type of member.
- A "_property_" is:
	- A member variable declared **in GDScript** (with the `var` keyword in the class body).
	- A member variable exposed with `ADD_PROPERTY`
	- almost everything present in the array returned by `Object.get_property_list` (hold to that thought)

For most practical use-cases, what matters most is that a property is a member, but a member is **not always** a property. This distinction is very similar to "method" vs. "function".
But in some cases it is worth being more specific because, as the prior explanations imply:

- A "member variable" points to an actual space in memory, so to speak.
- A dynamic/custom/fake property be exposed via `Object._get_property_list` and similar methods
	- This means a property is oftentimes associated with a member variable, but that's **not always the case**.

[Ideally a similar tweak should also be applied in `godot-docs`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/pull/12182)

Yes, the class reference's `member` tag is still named that way for legacy reasons.

[^1]: I recall that local constants are not purely local, but this is an internal detail.
